title: Sets and maps: a first guide
summary: Sets, maps, and their basic rules, with plain explanations, examples, and questions.
abstract: Sets describe collections of objects, and maps describe rules that assign one output to each input. Together they give a precise language for tracking how collections change: a map sends a chosen set of inputs to a set of outputs, and each set of outputs determines the inputs that lead to it. When every allowed output has exactly one input, this correspondence works in both directions and the map has an inverse.
